_why: The household words for a room this site names differently. Every entry is measured, not guessed: the 'queries' and 'covered' figures are from ops/keyword-demand.json's 2026-10-02 harvest, which ran the VOCABULARY_PROBES seeds added to ops/keyword_demand.py for exactly this question. A word earns a place here only if people type it AND this site does not already answer for it.
_rule: Do not add a word with no measured queries. 'master closet', 'rec room', 'ensuite' and 'lounge' were all considered and all returned zero, so naming them would be inventing demand. Do not add a word the site already covers: 'linen closet' (51 queries, 24 covered), 'coat closet' (21, 11), 'walk in closet' (34, 15) and 'front hall' (6, 4) are all answered already and adding them would be noise. 'utility room' was wrongly kept on this list until 2026-10-31: its 'covered' queries scored against /articles/how-to-organize-a-basement.html, matched only because that page's own unrelated headings happen to carry both words ('3. The utility zone: keep it clear' and '6. The room you actually use'), not because the Laundry Room, the real answer, said anything about being a utility room at all. See the Laundry Room entry below.

Kids Bedroom.source: Found 2026-11-06, scheduled operator cycle, mining Primary Bedroom's partial tier (ops/room_guide_underperformance.py --room 'Primary Bedroom'): 'boys bedroom organization ideas', 'how to organize a boys bedroom', 'how to organise a boys bedroom', 'childrens bedroom organization ideas', 'how to organise a girls bedroom', 'how to declutter children's bedroom' and 'how to organize a small children's bedroom' (7 unique queries, 10 rows across both harvests) all scored partial against /articles/how-to-declutter-a-bedroom.html (Primary Bedroom's own guide), unmatched only on the child word each time. REMOVED 2026-11-19, scheduled operator cycle: 'childrens bedroom' (no apostrophe) now matches zero of the current harvest, test_room_also_called.py's own evidence rule FAILing CI (checks.yml run 44547908641). Root cause checked directly, not assumed: keyword-demand.yml was narrowed to '--source google' earlier the same day (Bing's osjson.aspx returning HTTP 204 to its own canary), and this no-apostrophe row was apparently Bing-only; the apostrophe form 'children's bedroom' still has real evidence (ops/keyword-demand-global.json: 'children's bedroom organization ideas', 'how to declutter children's bedroom'), so it stays. Removing the ungrounded form now rather than leave a currently-false claim live; re-add once '--source both' is restored and it re-earns evidence. This is the exact A25/A26 Guest-vs-Primary tie-break shape, not a new bug: the purpose-built page for this already exists and already answers the identical plain phrasing perfectly ('kids bedroom organization ideas' and six siblings score covered at /articles/how-to-organize-a-kids-bedroom.html, grep-confirmed, zero relation invented here), but with no room signal for 'boys'/'girls'/'childrens'/children's', the exact-score tie (both pages match on the bare word 'bedroom' alone) falls to url order, and 'declutter' sorts before 'organize'. Checked the losing page honestly before naming this a misroute, not assumed: how-to-declutter-a-bedroom.html does carry a real, relevant section ('A very messy room, or a child's room') that answers the general decluttering process for a child's room, so routing a plain 'child's bedroom' singular query there (already covered, left alone) is not wrong. The four names added here are specifically the ones a parent of a boy, a girl, or children (plural) types, which is Kids Bedroom's own already-published subject, not this article's. 'kids bedroom design ideas for girls' was checked and correctly excluded: the substring 'girls bedroom' does not appear in it ('ideas for girls', different word order), and that query already scores partial at the correct kids-bedroom page, a different, smaller gap (unmatched 'design'/'girls') left for a future cycle. Verified against the real household_room_signal()/_tie_break() mechanism in ops/keyword_demand.py (A26) before adding, not assumed: both candidate pages are curated ROOM_GUIDES entries, so room_of() via guide_article_rooms() already tags them Primary Bedroom and Kids Bedroom respectively, and _tie_break() prefers the page matching a detected room signal on an exact score tie, which this is.

Home Office.source: ops/keyword-demand-global.json 2026-11-01 (ca): 'home office organization tips for creating a productive workspace', rank 12, gap, 0.333 coverage, scored to /home-office-deck.html. 'Workspace' is the plain household word for this room; the page carried no 'workspace' wording anywhere (grep-confirmed) before this entry. 'Creating', 'productive' and 'tips' stay unmatched: generic listicle filler, not facts this product states about the room, the same discipline 'plan'/'design' were held to in the Room layout tips.

Entryway.source_hallway: ops/keyword-demand-global.json 2026-11-05, ops/keyword-demand.json: 29 queries containing 'hallway' across both harvests, most already covered against Hall Closet's own longer 'hallway closet' synonym (which wins the room-signal tie by length per household_room_signal's longest-match rule, so no collision). Four remain partial with the bare word 'hallway' unmatched: 'hallway coat closet organization ideas' (content words hallway/coat/closet, already carrying 'coat'+'closet' from the entryway article, only 'hallway' missing), 'how to declutter hallway', 'how to decorate a small entrance hallway' (already carries the 'entrance hall' room signal, 'small' stays a separate cross-room modifier), and 'hallway cabinet organization ideas' (checked and left alone: a hallway storage cabinet is a genuine word-sense ambiguity with nothing this site answers, not improved by this entry). Grep-confirmed before this edit: no page's title or h1-h3 headings carried 'hallway' except Hall Closet's own pages, so this is not already covered elsewhere and cannot collide with them (the Hall Closet synonym 'hallway closet' is a longer string and always wins the household_room_signal tie-break when both appear).

Pantry.source: 'groceries' added 2026-11-15, scheduled operator cycle, mining Family Room's remaining 14%-uncovered partial tier (ops/room_guide_underperformance.py). 'large storage boxes for organizing groceries' (ops/keyword-demand.json, partial, 0.333 coverage) was tied 2-of-3 content words between the Pantry Backstock and Bulk Zone (storage+groceries, after this same cycle added 'groceries zone' to ops/zone-also-called.json) and Family Room's Board Game and Puzzle Zone (storage+boxes), with no room signal to break the cross-room tie, so it kept routing to the wrong room. REMOVED 2026-11-19, scheduled operator cycle: 'groceries' now matches zero of the current harvest (test_room_also_called.py FAILing CI, checks.yml run 44547908641), the same keyword-demand.yml '--source google' side effect named on the Kids Bedroom entry above; this signal_name was apparently Bing-only evidence. Removed rather than leave a currently-ungrounded signal live; re-add once '--source both' is restored and it re-earns evidence. Checked ops/zone-also-called.json's own 'groceries zone' entry (Pantry|Backstock and Bulk Zone) for the same exposure rather than assume it was unaffected: the same root query is now also absent from both corpora (0 of either file matches '\bgrocer'), so that entry is removed in the same commit, for the same reason. Not added as a plain 'names' entry: Pantry is not 'also called the Groceries', it is where groceries are stored, so this is a signal_names entry (the A140/Nursery precedent), read by room_synonyms() for scoring only, never rendered as an 'Also called' heading (also_called_html() and gate_also_called_is_heading read only 'names'). Checked for the exact collision this precedent warns about before adding: the only other grocery-related row in either corpus is 'grocery organizer for car' (singular 'grocery', already correctly scored to the Garage's Automotive Care Zone). household_room_signal()'s own word-boundary regex (\bgroceries s?\b-shaped, an exact word plus an optional trailing s) matches the plural 'groceries' in the target query but cannot match the singular 'grocery' in the car-organizer row, confirmed directly rather than assumed, so adding the plural form alone creates no collision with that row or any other.

Stair Landing.source: REMOVED 'stairway landing' 2026-11-19, scheduled operator cycle: it now matches zero of the current harvest (test_room_also_called.py FAILing CI, checks.yml run 44547908641), the same keyword-demand.yml '--source google' side effect named on the Kids Bedroom and Pantry entries above. 'staircase landing' keeps real evidence (ops/keyword-demand.json 'staircase landing storage ideas'; ops/keyword-demand-global.json 'staircase landing area decor', 'staircase landing storage ideas', 'staircase landing structure'), so it stays. Removing the ungrounded form now rather than leave a currently-false claim live; re-add once '--source both' is restored and it re-earns evidence.

Hall Closet.source: ops/keyword-demand-global.json 2026-10-23 (gb, au, in) for 'hall cupboard'. 'hallway closet' added 2026-11-04, scheduled operator cycle: 'how to organize a deep hallway closet' and 'how to organize a small hallway closet' (both tiers) plus 'small hallway closet organization ideas' (global) all score 'partial' (0.667) against an unrelated page (how-to-organize-a-linen-closet.html or how-to-organize-a-laundry-room.html) via a tied word-overlap collision on 'organize'/'closet' alone, the same alphabetical-tie-break shape A25/A26/A37 already named, because no Hall Closet page carries the word 'hallway' anywhere in a heading. Most 'hallway closet' queries already score 'covered' against hall-closet-deck.html, which does carry 'hallway' (card headings about a hallway chair and a toddler loose in the hallway) and 'closet', confirming this is the real room; the three partial rows differ only in using 'deep'/'small', which do not change the real destination. The room's own intro ('the hall closet is the darkest and deepest storage in the house') and name already describe exactly this closet in the hallway, so 'hallway closet' is the plain household name for it, not an invented one. 'under stairs cupboard' added 2026-11-05, scheduled operator cycle, continuing entry 131's handoff to mine the 'stairs' cluster the global harvest's partial rows surfaced: 'how to organise under stairs cupboard' (gb), 'how to organise under stairs storage' (gb) and 'how to organize closet under stairs' (gb, au, ca, in) all score 'partial' with only the bare word 'stairs' unmatched, against wrong pages (a kitchen cabinet zone, a generic downloads page) because no page anywhere names this space. The British/Commonwealth cupboard under the stairs is the same real storage space this room's own intro already describes ('the darkest and deepest storage in the house'), the household catch-all closet for vacuum, cleaning supplies and seasonal gear, not a separate room; checked against content.json before adding (Cleaning Equipment Zone, Cleaning Supply Zone and Seasonal and Guest Zone all match what this space actually holds). Named 'under stairs cupboard' rather than the more natural 'understairs cupboard' or 'cupboard under the stairs' for two reasons found in sequence, both checked directly rather than assumed: the compound 'understairs cupboard' rebuilt clean but moved zero rows on rescore, because the scorer's word() tokenizer treats 'understairs' as one token, not a match for the query token 'stairs' (the same literal-word-not-stem bar A34/A36 already learned for nappy/nappies and craft/crafts); 'cupboard under the stairs' then failed test_room_also_called.py's own evidence check, because that exact phrase appears in zero harvested queries, only reordered variants do. 'under stairs cupboard' is the literal substring of the real harvested query 'how to organise under stairs cupboard', satisfying both the evidence test and the tokenizer. Re-rescored and confirmed moved before shipping. Grep-confirmed before this edit: no page's title or h1-h3 headings anywhere on the site carried 'stairs' except Stair Landing's own pages, which are about the landing surface and floor path, not storage, so no content-based collision.

All 26 global queries plus 15 more in the US harvest (ops/keyword-demand.json) were scoring 'covered' or 'partial' against /articles/how-to-organize-a-basement.html or /articles/how-long-does-it-take-to-organise-a-room.html, neither of which is about this room; 'covered' is recorded as 0 here because none of that was earned by a Laundry Room page, which carried no 'utility room' wording at all until this entry.

Patio or Deck.source: ops/keyword-demand-global.json 2026-10-29 (in) for 'terrace'; 2026-10-31 (au) for 'backyard'; 2026-11-01 (gb) for 'porch'. 'backyard organisation' (rank 7, au) scored 'gap' against /about.html on a coincidental title match, not because that page is about this room; the Patio or Deck page's own six zones (seating, grilling, dining, garden, storage, the surface/rail/safety zone) are exactly what a household means by 'backyard', and the page carried no 'backyard' wording at all until this entry. 'porch organisation' (rank 10, gb) scored 'gap' against /about.html the same way; 'porch' is the plain British/Commonwealth word for the same outdoor seating structure this room already covers, confirmed by grep: neither the room page nor the deck page carried the word at all before this entry. Thin evidence (one query each) but real, not invented.

Mudroom.source: ops/keyword-demand.json 2026-11-05, ops/room_guide_underperformance.py --room Mudroom: 'how to organize mudroom lockers' (partial, 0.5 title coverage) and 'mudroom locker organization ideas' (partial, 0.5 title coverage), both already scored to this room's own pages (mudroom-deck.html or a zone page) via the word 'mudroom', only 'lockers'/'locker' unmatched. Neither word appeared anywhere in this site's titles or h1-h3 headings before this entry (grep-confirmed, including the sample-chapters download, where 'locker' appears once in body prose about a rented storage locker, not a heading). A built-in mudroom locker system, assigned hooks plus a cubby or bench per person, is exactly what the Family Hook Zone and Bench and Transition Surface already describe; it names the whole room's built-in system, not one specific zone, the same shape as 'porch'/'terrace' above, so it belongs at room level. Both the plural and singular forms are added because the scorer does no stemming (confirmed in ops/keyword_demand.py's own _morphology_variants docstring: it is used only for tie-break near-miss credit, never the primary score), and each form matches a different real query. Thin evidence (one query per form) but real, not invented. **Corrected 2026-11-26, PM check-in (~14:1x slot): removed 'lockers' (plural).** The 2026-11-26 weekly global harvest's autocomplete snapshot no longer carries 'how to organize mudroom lockers' or any other query containing 'lockers' in either corpus (confirmed by direct grep of both committed files, zero matches), so `gate_room_also_called_evidence` correctly FAILed on push. 'locker' (singular) still has a live grounding query in both corpora ('mudroom locker organization ideas') and is kept. Rescored after removal: 0 best_page/status changes in either corpus, since 'locker' alone already carried every row this name mattered for.

Nursery.source: Found 2026-11-15, scheduled operator cycle, investigating the A87 handoff ('dresser for newborn', 'weekend diaper bag organizer', 'baby clothes in small space' misrouting to Guest Bedroom/Kids Bedroom pages). 'baby clothes' and 'diaper bag' are not other words for the room 'Nursery' the way 'master bedroom' is for Primary Bedroom, so they are 'signal_names', not 'names': ops/keyword_demand.py's room_synonyms() now reads both, but also_called_html() and gate_also_called_is_heading read only 'names', so this entry can never force a false 'Also called the diaper bag' claim onto the live Nursery room page (CLAUDE.md section 8). 60 queries across both corpora contain one of the two phrases (43 already 'covered' or 'partial' on some page, so this is a misattribution fix, not a coverage fix). Verified with a full before/after score_rows()-shaped diff across both corpora (2,810 US + 2,166 global rows) before shipping, not assumed: adding the two signal_names changes best_page/status on exactly 2 rows ('weekend diaper bag organizer': /guest-bedroom-deck.html -> /nursery-deck.html; 'what to keep in diaper bag': /articles/how-to-organize-a-kids-bedroom.html -> /nursery-deck.html), both genuine corrections, 0 status changes, 0 rows moved to a worse or wrong page anywhere in either corpus. The harder A87 row, 'how to organize baby clothes in small space', is NOT fixed by this: Guest Bedroom's own Guest Dresser zone genuinely discusses 'a bag of outgrown baby clothes' in its own content (a real household friction about hand-me-downs, not a scorer bug), so it out-scores Nursery's Baby Clothing Zone on raw word overlap (0.75 vs 0.5) even with the room signal now set; _prefer_in_room_zone() only overrides a tied or cross-room ARTICLE, never a higher-scoring cross-room ZONE, and widening that to zones generically was checked and declined: zones are single-topic pages by design, so a zone's higher score is ordinarily the more trustworthy signal, not the less trustworthy one the article-only override exists to discount. Left exactly as diagnosed by the prior cycle (15-way tie on the bare word 'dresser' alone, no safe narrow fix), not papered over; this entry closes the two rows that were safely fixable and leaves the rest named rather than forced.

Kitchen.source: Found 2026-11-22, PM check-in (~06:4x slot), reading Primary Bedroom's room-guide partial tier: 'how to organize bags of spices' (global, ca) scored a 0.5/0.5 tie between /articles/how-to-declutter-a-bedroom.html (matched the coincidental word 'bags', from an unrelated heading 'Before you start: three bags and a time limit') and /zones/kitchen-the-cooking-zone.html (matched the word 'spices', which is already literally in that zone's own heading, 'The spice rack you are not honest about', and in its content.json purpose/sustain text). No room signal existed for either page, so the tie fell to alphabetical URL order ('/articles/...' before '/zones/...'), the same shape A25/A26/A74/A197 already name. 'spices' is not another name for the room 'Kitchen' the way 'master bedroom' is for Primary Bedroom (a household would never say 'also called the spices'), so this is a 'signal_names' entry, the same Nursery precedent above, not a 'names' entry: it cannot reach also_called_html() or gate_also_called_is_heading, so no false 'Also called' claim can result. Checked collision first (CLAUDE.md 5c/5d): 'spice' appears in exactly one query across both corpora (this one) and in exactly one heading sitewide (the Cooking Zone's own), so this entry can only ever affect this single row. Verified with a real before/after score_rows() rescore on both corpora: global corpus, 1 row changes, best_page corrected from the bedroom article to /zones/kitchen-the-cooking-zone.html, status unchanged at 'partial' (0.5, now via the room-signal tie-break rather than alphabetical order; 'bags' is still genuinely unmatched there, since this zone stores spices in a jar or rack, not a bag, so forcing the word 'bags' onto it would be the fabricated connection CLAUDE.md section 6 forbids), 0 regressions, US corpus unaffected (the query is global-only). A sibling row in the same tier, 'how to organize disposable bags' (unmatched 'disposable'), was checked and declined: no Kitchen or any other zone's real content is about disposable bags generically (trash bags, produce bags and storage bags are three different unrelated things), so no honest page exists to route it to; left as a genuine, named content gap, not forced.

_global_note: Entries carrying a 'source' were measured by ops/keyword_demand_global.py, which harvests the same seeds for gb, au, ca and in. ops/tests/test_room_also_called.py accepts evidence from either harvest.
